questions.q: What table holds the Update Set container record itself?
options: sys_update_xml
sys_update_set
sys_user
sys_properties
questions.explain: sys_update_set is the container; the individual captured changes inside it live on sys_update_xml.

questions.q: Which of these would actually be captured inside an active Update Set?
options: A new Incident submitted by an end user
A new user added to sys_user
A newly created Business Rule
A Change Request's state changing from New to Implement
questions.explain: Update Sets capture configuration/metadata changes like Business Rules -- never ordinary data records.

questions.q: An admin creates a UI Policy and, in the same session, ten test Incidents. What happens to the ten Incidents?
options: They are captured in the Update Set alongside the UI Policy
They are never captured in the Update Set, regardless of which one is active
They are captured only if the admin manually adds them
They are captured, but only the first five
questions.explain: Data records are never captured by an Update Set -- only configuration/metadata changes are, no matter what's active.

questions.q: Why does ServiceNow scope Update Sets strictly to configuration instead of also capturing data?
options: Data records are too large to store in sys_update_xml
So promoting a change to Production only ever changes behavior, never floods it with Dev's throwaway data
Because data records cannot be versioned at all
There is no real reason -- it's an arbitrary platform limitation
questions.explain: This scoping is exactly what prevents the kind of silent, accidental data copy the Instances & Environments lesson warned against.

questions.q: Which phrase best captures what an Update Set moves between instances, per this lesson?
options: "The data inside it"
"Every record on every table"
"How the system behaves"
"A full database backup"
questions.explain: Update Sets move behavior -- Business Rules, ACLs, policies, scripts -- never the data those behaviors act on.
